prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1214; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a side-impact collision at an intersection in Pasadena, Texas, where two vehicles met during a left turn across traffic. Driver 1 stated that the vehicle was struck on the driver's side as Driver 2 entered the intersection. Driver 2 acknowledged the collision and did not dispute the sequence of events described by Driver 1. Two independent witnesses on the sidewalk gave statements consistent with that account, and scene photographs match the reported point of impact. A Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time and was confirmed present by officers and both witnesses. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness shortly after the crash, and the nature of the impact appears consistent with that complaint given the force involved. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to officers or noted at the scene. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the applicable policy. Officers were unable to determine with certainty whether all of the visible damage resulted solely from this impact, and this question has been noted for follow-up.
